meta.name: Hydra SDK
meta.description: Architecture map of the Hydra SDK monorepo: a TypeScript toolkit for building Cardano + Hydra Layer 2 wallet applications.
meta.generatedFrom: static analysis of packages/*, apps/*, infra/* on branch master

tiers.app: Applications and consumers of the SDK
tiers.remote: Remote services reached over the network
tiers.infra: Local test infrastructure checked into the repo

nodes.label: Nuxt playground
nodes.desc: Nuxt 3 + Vue 3 interactive demo deployed to playground.hydrasdk.com. Pages cover the transaction builder, a Hydra tx trace viewer and raw cardano-wasm checks. Merging to master deploys it — never commit .output.

nodes.label: Node.js playground
nodes.desc: Integration scripts run against a real node: lock/unlock Plutus validators, mint and burn, key management, and the memory-leak harnesses that drove the WASM free-after-build work in TxBuilder.

nodes.label: Docs site
nodes.desc: Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI documentation at hydrasdk.com, English only, organised in five Diátaxis sections. apps/docs is the deprecated v1 site kept only for its URLs.

nodes.label: Your application
nodes.desc: Any wallet or dApp installing the published packages. Imports only through @hydra-sdk/* — the SDK never asks you to touch @emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib directly.

nodes.label: HydraBridge
nodes.desc: The single entry point to a Hydra head. Owns the connector, the snapshot caches, slot-zero derivation from Greetings, protocol parameters, auto-reconnect, and the whole command surface.

nodes.label: WebsocketConnector
nodes.desc: Default connector. Parses one URL into a socket URL and an HTTP base URL, appends history / snapshot-utxo / address query params, and ships a fetcher and submitter that hit the hydra-node REST API directly.

nodes.label: HexcoreConnector
nodes.desc: Alternative connector for a Hexcore gateway in front of the node. Implements the same HydraConnector contract with every route prefixed /hydra, so HydraBridge cannot tell the difference.

nodes.label: Event bus
nodes.desc: The connector's mitt emitter, re-exposed as bridge.events. Emits onConnected, onDisconnected, onConnectError and onMessage — every server payload arrives here already narrowed by tag.

nodes.label: Snapshot cache
nodes.desc: Two maps rebuilt O(n) once per snapshot: address → txHash → UTxO, and address → assetUnit → bigint. lastSnapshotNumber guards them so a slow HTTP reply can never overwrite fresher WebSocket data.

nodes.label: Payload & tags
nodes.desc: The discriminated union for every hydra-node server output, plus the HydraCommand and HydraHeadStatus enums. Derived from the Haskell source and verified against a live 2.3.0 node by the e2e suite.

nodes.label: awaitHydraMessage
nodes.desc: Turns the node's fire-and-forget socket into promises: subscribes to onMessage, resolves on the matching success tag, rejects on TxInvalid, CommandFailed, PostTxOnChainFailed or RejectedInputBecauseUnsynced, and always clears its timer.

nodes.label: Head commands
nodes.desc: The client-input surface of the head, serialised onto the socket: open it, move value inside it, take value out, or wind it down.

nodes.label: TxBuilder
nodes.desc: Stages inputs, outputs, mints, certificates, withdrawals, validity and metadata as plain descriptors, then assembles them into CSL in one pass at complete(). Knows about Hydra: isHydra skips the L1 fee and collateral rules.

nodes.label: datumBuilder
nodes.desc: Fluent construction of PlutusData from primitives (int, bytes), collections (list, map) and structured constr values, without hand-rolling CSL calls.

nodes.label: buildRedeemer
nodes.desc: Builds a Redeemer from a JS value with an explicit tag (SPEND, MINT, CERT, REWARD), pointer index and execution-unit budget. emptyRedeemer() covers validators that ignore their argument.

nodes.label: Metadata encoder
nodes.desc: Recursively converts JS values — strings, numbers, bigints, byte arrays, arrays, objects and Maps — into TransactionMetadatum, with bigint-safe JSON helpers alongside.

nodes.label: AppWallet
nodes.desc: The wallet most applications use. Accepts a root bech32 key, cardano-cli key files or a mnemonic; holds an optional fetcher and submitter so querying and submitting go through one object.

nodes.label: EmbeddedWallet
nodes.desc: The key-handling layer AppWallet delegates to. WalletStaticMethods turns a mnemonic into a root private key and cardano-cli hex keys into signing keys; the instance derives accounts and returns raw Vkeywitnesses.

nodes.label: CardanoCliWallet
nodes.desc: Wallet backed by cardano-cli .skey envelopes. Since core 1.5.0 those keys are derived as BIP32-Ed25519 extended keys so signatures match what the node expects.

nodes.label: BuildKeys
nodes.desc: CIP-1852 derivation (m/1852'/1815'/account'/role/index) and address construction: base, enterprise, reward and DRep identifiers, plus scalar clamping and extended-key stripping.

nodes.label: Serializer / Deserializer
nodes.desc: The CBOR boundary. Reads transactions, addresses, Plutus scripts and Plutus data out of hex, writes asset units back, and extracts the amounts a transaction moves.

nodes.label: Resolver
nodes.desc: Computes the transaction id from a CBOR hex string or a TransactionBody — the identity every Hydra event is keyed by, available before the transaction is ever submitted.

nodes.label: Converter
nodes.desc: Translates between the array shape the builder wants and the keyed map shape Hydra snapshots use, and turns a TxOutput descriptor into a CSL TransactionOutput.

nodes.label: Domain helpers
nodes.desc: The namespaced helpers re-exported from the package root: datum hashing, policy ids and native scripts, applying parameters to Plutus scripts, and address derivation and inspection.

nodes.label: Providers
nodes.desc: Chain access behind two small interfaces. BaseWalletProvider fixes the contract; Blockfrost, Ogmios and Demeter implementations ship with the package, and anything satisfying IFetcher/ISubmitter can replace them.

nodes.label: Protocol & constants
nodes.desc: Default protocol parameters, Plutus cost models and network ids. defaultCostModels is a getter, not a constant — building it eagerly would run WASM while core is still being imported and race the bundler's async instantiation.

nodes.label: Parser · Time · Metadata
nodes.desc: Hex, byte and text conversion; slot-to-time arithmetic the bridge uses once slot zero is known; and transaction metadata helpers.

nodes.label: Validation
nodes.desc: Address and output checks used before a transaction reaches CSL, where a bad value costs an opaque WASM panic instead of a readable error. ValidatorUtils is the deprecated alias.

nodes.label: @hydra-sdk/cardano-wasm
nodes.desc: The only module allowed to import @emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib. package.json export conditions pick the build — the consumer's bundler or runtime decides, not a runtime branch.

nodes.label: CSL · browser
nodes.desc: Resolved by the browser export condition. WASM is instantiated asynchronously by the bundler, which is why core must not touch it at import time.

nodes.label: CSL · Node.js
nodes.desc: Resolved by the node export condition, via src/index.node.ts. Used by the Node playground, the test suite and any server-side consumer.

nodes.label: CSL · asm.js
nodes.desc: Fallback for environments that cannot instantiate WASM. Opt-in only, through the /asmjs subpath — never selected automatically.

nodes.label: hydra-node · WebSocket
nodes.desc: The head's live channel. Greetings on connect, then a stream of TimedServerOutput payloads; client inputs go back the same way. Query params control history, snapshot-utxo and address filtering.

nodes.label: hydra-node · REST
nodes.desc: The node's request/response surface, used for cold-start reads and for anything that needs a reported outcome rather than a fire-and-forget command.

nodes.label: Hexcore · REST
nodes.desc: A gateway that fronts one or more hydra nodes with the same routes under a /hydra prefix, plus API-key headers. Swapping to it is a connector change, not an application change.

nodes.label: hydra-offline devnet
nodes.desc: A hydra-node in offline mode with a seeded UTxO set — no L1 at all. The e2e suite runs against it on port 4002. Commit, decommit, fanout and contest cannot be exercised here; those need a devnet with a cardano-node.

nodes.label: hydra-preprod
nodes.desc: An online head on the preprod network, backed by a real cardano-node. This is where the L1-facing half of the lifecycle — commit, fanout, contest — is actually testable.

nodes.label: Cardano L1
nodes.desc: The settlement layer. Commits deposit into the head's script, decommits decrement it, and fanout distributes the final snapshot. The SDK never speaks to it directly — the hydra node or a provider does.

nodes.label: Blockfrost
nodes.desc: The default L1 provider. Pages address UTxOs, normalises them into the SDK's UTxO shape, and submits signed transactions.

nodes.label: Ogmios / Demeter
nodes.desc: A direct bridge to a cardano-node. Beyond UTxO queries and submission it can evaluate a transaction, which is what supplies TxBuilder with real Plutus execution units.

flows.name: Create a wallet from a mnemonic
flows.tagline: Twenty-four words become an account, three addresses and a signing key.

steps.title: Construct the wallet
steps.note: new AppWallet({ networkId, key: { type: 'mnemonic', words } }). The same constructor also takes a root bech32 key or a pair of cardano-cli keys.

steps.title: Pick the key strategy
steps.note: The constructor switches on key.type and hands the material to the embedded layer. Nothing is derived yet.

steps.title: Mnemonic → root private key
steps.note: WalletStaticMethods.mnemonicToPrivateKeyHex runs BIP39 entropy through Bip32PrivateKey.from_bip39_entropy with the supplied password.

steps.title: Derive the account
steps.note: buildKeys walks m/1852'/1815'/account'/role/index and returns the payment key, stake key and the base, enterprise and reward addresses in one object.

steps.title: Cross the WASM boundary
steps.note: Bip32PrivateKey, Credential and BaseAddress are CSL types; this is the only module that imports them.

steps.title: Resolve the right build
steps.note: The bundler's browser condition selects the browser WASM build. In Node the node condition wins instead — no runtime branch is involved.

flows.name: Build, sign and submit on L1
flows.tagline: The ordinary Cardano path, from UTxO query to transaction id.

steps.title: Start from the wallet
steps.note: One AppWallet carries the key, the fetcher and the submitter, so querying, signing and submitting all go through it.

steps.title: Query spendable UTxOs
steps.note: queryUTxOs(address) throws unless a fetcher was supplied — the wallet never invents chain access.

steps.title: Reach the chain
steps.note: BlockfrostProvider satisfies both IFetcher and ISubmitter, so a single object covers reads and writes.

steps.title: Fetch and normalise
steps.note: GET /addresses/{address}/utxos is paged until exhausted, then each entry is mapped into the SDK's UTxO shape.

steps.title: Stage the transaction
steps.note: setInputs(utxos) → txOut(address, amount) → changeAddress(addr) → complete(). Every call stages a descriptor; nothing touches CSL yet.

steps.title: Size the fee
steps.note: minFeeA, minFeeB, coinsPerUtxoSize and the cost models come from the protocol parameters passed to the builder.

steps.title: Assemble and build
steps.note: _assembleAndBuild pours the staged parts into CSL's TransactionBuilder and calls add_change_if_needed, then build_tx.

steps.title: Learn the transaction id
steps.note: resolveTxHash(cborHex) gives the id before submission — worth recording, because that is the key every later event uses.

steps.title: Sign
steps.note: signTx builds a Vkeywitness through EmbeddedWallet and re-attaches it to the FixedTransaction, preserving the original body bytes.

steps.title: Submit
steps.note: POST /tx/submit returns the transaction id the node accepted. Compare it with step 8 as a cheap sanity check.

steps.title: Settle
steps.note: The transaction is in the mempool; confirmation follows chain timing, not SDK timing.

flows.name: Connect to a Hydra head
flows.tagline: One URL, a socket, and the Greetings message that seeds everything.

steps.title: Open the bridge
steps.note: new HydraBridge({ url: 'ws://localhost:4001', history: false }) — or pass your own connector instead of a url.

steps.title: Wire the listeners
steps.note: The constructor subscribes to onConnected and onMessage before the socket opens, so no Greetings can be missed.

steps.title: Split the URL
steps.note: parseUrl produces both a socket URL and an HTTP base URL from the one input, and appends history, snapshot-utxo and address query params.

steps.title: Socket opens
steps.note: The node sends Greetings immediately. Unlike every other server output it carries no seq or timestamp, and its env deliberately omits the signing key.

steps.title: Narrow the payload
steps.note: Raw JSON is narrowed to the HydraPayload union by its tag; InvalidInput is reshaped because the node sends it without one.

steps.title: Emit
steps.note: onConnected fires first, then onMessage for every payload. bridge.events is this emitter.

steps.title: Seed the state
steps.note: Greetings sets nodeVersion, syncedStatus and an approximate slotZeroTimestamp, superseded later by an exact chainSlot/chainTime pair.

steps.title: Cold-start fallback
steps.note: querySnapshotUtxo() runs GET /snapshot/utxo in the background and is discarded if a WebSocket snapshot arrived first — lastSnapshotNumber decides.

steps.title: Where to try it
steps.note: pnpm hydra:offline brings up a seeded offline node on :4002 with no L1 attached — enough for connect, submit and snapshot flows.

flows.name: Commit funds into the head
flows.tagline: An incremental deposit: draft on the node, sign locally, settle on L1.

steps.title: Choose what to move in
steps.note: Pick the L1 UTxOs to deposit, or supply a blueprint transaction when the commit needs a script witness.

steps.title: Ask the node to draft it
steps.note: bridge.commit(data) forwards straight to connector.submitter.commit — the bridge adds no logic here.

steps.title: POST /commit
steps.note: Sent on the node's HTTP port, not the socket, because the caller needs the drafted transaction back.

steps.title: Receive the draft
steps.note: The node returns an unsigned deposit transaction as cborHex. It is not yet valid — it has no witnesses.

steps.title: Sign the draft
steps.note: signTx with the committing key. This is the point where custody stays on your side: the node never sees the key.

steps.title: Settle the deposit
steps.note: POST /cardano-transaction relays the signed deposit to L1. The node observes it and starts the deposit period.

steps.title: Track it by tag
steps.note: CommitRecorded → DepositActivated → CommitApproved → CommitFinalized arrive over the socket. A deposit that stalls stays listed in GET /commits.

steps.title: It appears in the head
steps.note: Once finalised the funds show up in the next SnapshotConfirmed and land in the address index.

flows.name: Send a transaction inside the head
flows.tagline: No fee, no collateral, no block — confirmation in a round trip.

steps.title: Read the head's UTxO set
steps.note: bridge.queryAddressUTxO(address) serves from the snapshot index; there is no L1 query in this flow at all.

steps.title: Take the head's parameters
steps.note: getProtocolParameters() returns what the node reports, which in most head configurations means zero fees.

steps.title: Build for Hydra
steps.note: new TxBuilder({ params, isHydra: true }) skips the L1 fee and collateral rules and lets change balance exactly.

steps.title: Build the transaction
steps.note: Same CSL path as L1 — a Hydra transaction is an ordinary Conway transaction, only the validation context differs.

steps.title: Sign
steps.note: Signed by the owner of the inputs. Head parties sign the snapshot, not your transaction.

steps.title: Submit and wait
steps.note: bridge.submitTxSync(tx) sends a NewTx command and blocks until the node answers, instead of the fire-and-forget commands.newTx.

steps.title: The head agrees
steps.note: The node broadcasts to the other parties; TxValid comes back keyed by transactionId.

steps.title: Resolve or reject
steps.note: Resolves on TxValid. Rejects on TxInvalid, on CommandFailed, and on RejectedInputBecauseUnsynced when the echoed client input is our own NewTx.

steps.title: Balances move
steps.note: SnapshotConfirmed rebuilds the address index and balance cache, so the next getAddressBalance already reflects the transfer.

flows.name: Read balances in O(1)
flows.tagline: Why the bridge keeps two maps instead of asking the node.

steps.title: SnapshotConfirmed arrives
steps.note: Carries the full confirmed UTxO set plus its snapshotNumber — a complete state, not a delta.

steps.title: Narrow and emit
steps.note: Parsed, tagged and pushed onto the emitter. The connector holds no state of its own.

steps.title: onMessage
steps.note: Both the bridge's internal handler and any application listener see the same payload.

steps.title: Guard against staleness
steps.note: updateSnapshot() compares snapshotNumber with lastSnapshotNumber, so a slow HTTP reply can never overwrite fresher WebSocket data.

steps.title: Reshape the UTxO set
steps.note: Hydra sends a keyed map; the builder wants an array. Converter owns both directions so neither side has to care.

steps.title: Rebuild both indexes
steps.note: One O(n) pass produces address → txHash → UTxO and address → assetUnit → bigint. The cost is paid once per snapshot, not once per query.

steps.title: Query for free
steps.note: getAddressBalance(addr) is a map lookup. null means the cache is cold — fall back to your own store; an empty Map means the address is in the head with nothing in it.

flows.name: Spend a Plutus script UTxO
flows.tagline: Two build passes, because the fee depends on the execution units.

steps.title: Locate the locked UTxO
steps.note: The script address holds the value; you supply the datum it was locked with and the redeemer that unlocks it.

steps.title: Compose the datum
steps.note: datumBuilder() assembles constr, list, map, int and bytes into PlutusData without hand-writing CSL calls.

steps.title: Compose the redeemer
steps.note: buildRedeemer(value, { tag: 'SPEND', index }) — or emptyRedeemer() for a validator that ignores its argument.

steps.title: Stage the script spend
steps.note: spendingPlutusScript('V3') → txInScript(cbor) or txInReference(txHash, ix) → txInRedeemerValue(r) → txInCollateral(...) → requiredSignerHash(...).

steps.title: Cost models and script data
steps.note: The language view and cost models feed the script data hash; a mismatch here is the classic cause of an unexplained script failure.

steps.title: First pass
steps.note: A draft transaction is built with the placeholder execution units carried on the staged redeemers.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.note: evaluator.evaluateTx(txHex) returns the real mem and steps budget for each redeemer pointer. Without an evaluator the single-pass build is returned as is — which is the normal case inside a head.

steps.title: Second pass
steps.note: _applyEvaluatedExUnits remaps SPEND results by input and MINT results by policy id, scales them by txEvaluationMultiplier, then rebuilds so CSL computes the correct fee.

steps.title: Sign
steps.note: Including every key named by requiredSignerHash, or the validator's signature check fails.

steps.title: Submit
steps.note: On L1 the script runs at validation time; the collateral is only consumed if it fails.

flows.name: Move funds back out of the head
flows.tagline: A decommit leaves the head open — unlike closing it.

steps.title: Decide what leaves
steps.note: A decommit withdraws specific UTxOs to L1 while everyone else keeps transacting inside the head.

steps.title: Build the decommit transaction
steps.note: Its outputs are the UTxOs you want back on L1. Build it against the head's parameters, then sign it.

steps.title: Request the decommit
steps.note: bridge.commands.decommit({ cborHex, txId, timeout }) — or POST /decommit through the connector's submitter when you want the HTTP form.

steps.title: Send it
steps.note: The Decommit client input goes out on the socket alongside everything else.

steps.title: The head decides
steps.note: DecommitRequested → DecommitApproved → DecommitFinalized. DecommitInvalid means the transaction was never accepted.

steps.title: Wait for approval
steps.note: Resolves on DecommitApproved matching our txId, so the caller gets a promise instead of an event subscription.

steps.title: Decrement on chain
steps.note: The node posts a decrement transaction that reduces the head's script UTxO and pays out the withdrawn value.

steps.title: The head shrinks
steps.note: The next snapshot no longer contains those UTxOs, and the balance cache reflects it on the same pass.

flows.name: Close the head and fan out
flows.tagline: The contestation window, then everything settles back to L1.

steps.title: Decide to wind down
steps.note: close() posts the latest snapshot on chain. safeClose() refuses when the node believes it is behind.

steps.title: Send Close
steps.note: bridge.commands.close(). From here the head is no longer accepting new transactions.

steps.title: HeadIsClosed
steps.note: Carries a contestation deadline. Until it passes, any party can contest with a newer snapshot.

steps.title: Watch the window
steps.note: HeadIsContested restarts the clock; ReadyToFanout means the deadline has passed and the head can be settled.

steps.title: Fan out
steps.note: commands.fanout() distributes the whole final snapshot. commands.partialFanout(utxo) settles a subset when the full set is too large for one transaction.

steps.title: Settle
steps.note: The fanout transaction pays every UTxO in the final snapshot back to its owner on L1.

steps.title: Confirm it is finished
steps.note: HeadIsFinalized arrives on the socket, and GET /head reports Idle again — the node is ready for a new head.

flows.name: Recover a stuck deposit
flows.tagline: Funds committed but never absorbed are still yours.

steps.title: Look for orphaned deposits
steps.note: Deposits stay recoverable after a head closes, so this is also how you reclaim funds from a previous head.

steps.title: List them
steps.note: pendingDeposits() calls GET /commits and throws a clear error when the connector does not implement it, rather than failing obscurely.

steps.title: The node answers
steps.note: Returns the txIds of deposits observed on chain but not yet included in any snapshot.

steps.title: Recover one
steps.note: recoverDeposit(txId) issues DELETE /commits/{txId}. It falls back to the Recover socket command when the connector has no HTTP form — but only the HTTP form reports the outcome.

steps.title: Funds return
steps.note: The deposit is spent back to the committing address on L1.

flows.name: Swap the node for a gateway
flows.tagline: The connector seam: the same bridge against a different backend.

steps.title: Pass a connector, not a URL
steps.note: new HydraBridge({ connector: new HexcoreConnector({ ... }) }). Everything downstream of this line is unchanged.

steps.title: The bridge cannot tell
steps.note: HydraBridge only ever touches connector.fetcher, connector.submitter, connector.eventEmitter and sendCommand — the whole HydraConnector contract.

steps.title: Same contract, different routes
steps.note: Every route is prefixed /hydra and an API-key header is attached; the method signatures are identical to the WebSocket connector's.

steps.title: The gateway
steps.note: GET /hydra/snapshot/utxo, POST /hydra/submit-tx, POST /hydra/transaction, DELETE /hydra/commits/{txId}.

steps.title: Still the same node
steps.note: The gateway proxies a real hydra node, so the payload union and its tags are unchanged.

steps.title: Caching is unaffected
steps.note: The cache lives in the bridge, above the seam, so it works identically whichever connector is underneath. Your own connector only has to satisfy HydraConnector.

flows.name: Sign with cardano-cli key files
flows.tagline: The envelope format a devnet hands you, read directly.

steps.title: Read the envelope
steps.note: The key-mgmt scripts load .skey files straight out of a devnet's credentials directory — no mnemonic involved.

steps.title: Construct the wallet
steps.note: new CardanoCliWallet({ key: { payment, stake } }) takes the cborHex from the envelope, not a bech32 string.

steps.title: Derive as extended keys
steps.note: Since core 1.5.0 cardano-cli keys are derived as BIP32-Ed25519 extended keys. Treating them as plain Ed25519 produced signatures the node rejected.

steps.title: Cross into CSL
steps.note: The extended private key and its public key both come from CSL, as does the witness.

steps.title: Witness without touching the body
steps.note: deserializeTx returns a FixedTransaction, so the witness is attached while the original body bytes — and therefore the transaction id — stay exactly as built.

steps.title: Where these keys come from
steps.note: infra/hydra-preprod and infra/hydra-offline both ship credentials in this format, which is why the SDK supports it at all.

flows.name: Mint and burn a native asset
flows.tagline: One policy, a positive quantity to mint and a negative one to burn.

steps.title: Start from the reference script
steps.note: apps/nodejs-playground/src/mint-burn-token.ts runs this end to end against a real node.

steps.title: Derive the policy id
steps.note: PolicyUtils turns a native script or a Plutus script into its policy id — the first half of every asset unit.

steps.title: Stage the mint
steps.note: mintingScript(script) → mint(quantity, policyId, assetName). A negative quantity burns; the burnt asset must be present in the inputs.

steps.title: Only for Plutus policies
steps.note: A Plutus minting policy needs a MINT redeemer indexed by the canonical policy-id ordering. A native script needs none.

steps.title: Attach CIP-25
steps.note: metadataValue(721, { ... }) encodes the token metadata; nested objects, Maps and bigints are all handled.

steps.title: Fail readably
steps.note: Outputs are checked before CSL sees them, so a malformed asset unit surfaces as an error message rather than an opaque WASM panic.

steps.title: Build
steps.note: The MintBuilder assembles the mint field and its witnesses, and the minted value is balanced into the change output.

steps.title: Sign
steps.note: With the policy key as well as the input keys, when the policy is a native script requiring a signature.

steps.title: Submit
steps.note: After confirmation the asset exists under policyId.assetName and can be spent like any other value.

flows.name: Keep WASM memory flat
flows.tagline: Why TxBuilder tracks and frees instead of trusting the collector.

steps.title: The symptom
steps.note: Under a burst of builds, memory climbs and throughput drops. The Node playground's leak harnesses reproduce it deliberately.

steps.title: Where it comes from
steps.note: CSL objects live in WASM linear memory. FinalizationRegistry does free them eventually, but not fast enough to keep up with a spike.

steps.title: Same on both builds
steps.note: The browser and Node builds share the allocation model, so the fix has to live above the boundary.

steps.title: Track, then free
steps.note: _track() records every transient object allocated during a build; _freeScratch() releases them in the finally block; the TransactionBuilder itself is freed after build_tx. Transaction 1.2.0 measured 0 KB per iteration after this.

steps.title: What you have to do
steps.note: Reuse one builder with reset() between transactions, or call dispose() when you are finished with it. A per-request builder that is never disposed reintroduces the problem.
